selected_evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 over the transit network
selected_evidence.summary: VyOS site-to-site peer NODE2 and OPNsense Swanctl connection/local/remote/child/PSK configured and committed; swanctl --list-sas on both node1 and node2 shows an ESTABLISHED IKEv2 SA and INSTALLED tunnel child SA between 172.16.0.1 and 172.16.0.2.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by private address with traffic encrypted in transit
selected_evidence.summary: node3 (10.50.1.2) pings node4 (10.50.2.2) and vice versa with 0% loss; node1's ESP SA counters increment from 0 to growing packet/byte counts concurrently with the pings, confirming the traffic traverses the encrypted tunnel rather than a direct path.

selected_evidence.requirement: Firewall/NAT allows the tunnel traffic (OPNsense default-deny)
selected_evidence.summary: Added OPNsense pass rules for IKE/NAT-T/ESP on opt1 and decrypted tunnel traffic to LAN_B on enc0; reloaded filter; confirmed node1 could then reach node2's LAN_B gateway address 10.50.2.1.

selected_evidence.requirement: Configuration persists (survives reboot) on VyOS and OPNsense
selected_evidence.summary: VyOS config committed+saved to config.boot; OPNsense interfaces/IPsec/firewall written directly to the live config.xml store (no separate save step required).
Captured node1 boot_id 32669db3-... and ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED IPsec SA state before restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command on node1 returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proven
selected_evidence.summary: node1 became unreachable (connection timed out) then returned with boot_id 4d7f696d-... , different from the pre-restart 32669db3-... baseline.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: recovered state and cluster function verified
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, eth1/eth2 addresses and the IPsec connection were present without reconfiguration, an ESTABLISHED SA and INSTALLED tunnel reappeared automatically, and node3 could ping node4 again.
Captured node2 kern.boottime (04:37:18), ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED IPsec SA, and pf enabled status before restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node2 returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: changed boot identity proven
selected_evidence.summary: node2 SSH became unreachable then returned with kern.boottime 04:54:48, different from the pre-restart 04:37:18 baseline.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: recovered state and cluster function verified
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, opt1/opt2 interfaces, pf (enabled), and an ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED IPsec SA all reappeared automatically without reconfiguration, and node4 could ping node3 again.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: limitation - recovery could not be confirmed
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command was acknowledged on node3, but after roughly 2 hours of repeated polling the node consistently returned 'connection reset by peer' and never became reachable again in this session, so its post-restart boot identity and recovery could not be verified.
